text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- In the last three years espionage against Norway has increased to at least the level of activity before the Berlin Wall fell, says outgoing security chief Ellen Holager Andenaes.

- The latest opinion poll by Norsk Gallup for TV2 shows that two out of five voters have still not decided how they will vote in September's election. The latest poll shows the Progress Party making headway among the electorate with 22.7 percent, while the Labour Party and the Conservatives have made only a little ground at 28.7 percent and 15.1 percent respectively.
- The central bank, Norges Bank, was received between 20 and 30 applications from companies wanting to manage the equity portfolio of Norway's Petroleum Fund.
- Furniture sales in the first half of the year increased by 14.4 percent, while total retail sales in the same period rose by 3.4 percent.
- Propertiy prices rose three percent between the first and second quarters of the year. Real estate agents believe prices will continue to rise.

- First-half revenues at state telecommunications company Telenor increased by 1.28 billion crowns compared with a year ago, largely due to higher traffic on mobile telephone networks. But operating profits at 1.27 billion crowns were 115 million crowns below the year-ago period due to a reduction in the prices of services.

- It is not the state's income that should decide its expenditure in a single year. The decisive factor is that the national budget should stimulate growth during recesssion and restrain growth during times of economic expansion, says Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg.
- State oil company Statoil has awarded the main contract for the planned seven billion crown expansion of the Kaarstoe gas treatment plant. The contract went to British group M. W. Kellogg Ltd.

- Kjell Magne Bondevik, candidate for the Christian People's Party to be Norway's next Prime Minister, has opened the possibility for a one percent levy on the trade of shares. Consequently there counld be a parliamentary majority for the proposal by the Socialist Venstre party, which would mean an additional two billion crowns in income each year to the state.
- Consumer prices fell by 0.2 percent in July from June and increased by 2.2 percent year-on-year, according to fidgures from Statistics Norway.

- People are using mobile phones more than ever despite that charges can be up to six times more expensive than conventional phones. In the first seven months of the year state telecommunications company Telenor increased GSM subscribers by 175,000 and now have a total of 710,000 GSM connections and 400,000 NMT subcribers.
